claim: SIA's chart of 2024 WSTS End Use Survey data puts automotive at 12.7% of global chip demand, third after computers/AI and communications.
evidence: Chart "TOTAL GLOBAL DEMAND SHARE BY END USE, 2024" (p. 24): PDF text layer has the label row "Automotive Government" directly above the value row "12.7% 1.0%" (same x positions); "Source: WSTS, 2024 End Use Survey"

metric.name: Automotive share of semiconductor demand
metric.methodology: WSTS End Use Survey, as charted by SIA

notes: Corrects CLM-0561 (which gave 9.9%; 9.9% is Consumer Electronics). Mapping read from the PDF text layer coordinates and confirmed visually. Consistent with CLM-1346 (automotive 'fell' to 10.9% in 2025).

claim: In 2024 communications accounted for 33.0%, consumer electronics 9.9%, industrial applications 8.4% and government 1.0% of global semiconductor demand (SIA, from the WSTS End Use Survey).
evidence: Chart "TOTAL GLOBAL DEMAND SHARE BY END USE, 2024" (p. 24), PDF text layer rows: "Computers/AI | Consumer Electronics" over "34.9% 9.9%"; "Communications Industrial Applications" over "33.0% 8.4%"; "Automotive Government" over "12.7% 1.0%"

metric.name: Communications share of semiconductor demand
metric.methodology: WSTS End Use Survey, as charted by SIA

notes: Resolves the label-mapping gap documented in CLM-0073 (unknown). Shares sum to 99.9% with Computers/AI 34.9% and Automotive 12.7%.

claim: TrendForce estimated TSMC's share of top-10 foundry revenue at 54.1% in 1Q20 (US$10.2 billion of US$18.06 billion); CSET (2021) cites this as TSMC's 54% share of the logic foundry market.
evidence: TrendForce table "Ranking of the Global Top 10 Foundries by Revenue, 1Q20": TSMC 1Q20E 10,200 (US$m), M/S 54.1%; Top 10 Total 18,060. CSET p.22: "Market leader TSMC has 54 percent of the world's logic foundry market share" (fn 76 cites this TrendForce release)

metric.name: TSMC share of top-10 foundry revenue
metric.population: Revenue of the top 10 foundries (Samsung incl. System LSI)
metric.methodology: TrendForce estimate compiled from company data

notes: Table read from the image on the TrendForce page (vision reading of a clear table). Newer: TrendForce 4Q25 70.4% (CLM-0068) and 2Q26 72.5% (CLM-0553).

claim: SIA/BCG estimated that chip design accounted for about 65% of 2019 semiconductor industry R&D excluding pre-competitive research, or 53% of total industry R&D including it.
evidence: p.22: "while 65% of the total industry R&D investment (excluding pre-competitive research) is made in the design layer"; p.15 sidebar: "Chip design 53% of industry R&D 13% of industry capex"; Exhibit 4: pre-competitive research "(15 to 20% of total industry R&D)"

metric.name: Design share of industry R&D (excl. pre-competitive research)
metric.population: Semiconductor industry R&D excluding pre-competitive research
metric.methodology: BCG analysis using Capital IQ and Gartner data

notes: Exhibit 4 activity R&D shares (design 53, front end 13, ATP 3, EDA/IP 3, equipment 9, materials 1) sum to 82%; 53/82 = 65%, so the two figures are consistent once the base is stated.

claim: SIA/BCG's Exhibit 4 and design sidebar put chip design at 50% of 2019 semiconductor industry value added.
evidence: p.15 sidebar: "Chip design 53% of industry R&D 13% of industry capex 50% of the value added"; Exhibit 4 (p.13) 'VALUE ADD' shares: design 50%, front end 24%, ATP 6%, EDA/IP 4%, equipment 11%, materials 5% (sum 100%)

metric.name: Design share of industry value added
metric.population: Value added across semiconductor value-chain activities ($290B)
metric.methodology: BCG analysis using Capital IQ and Gartner data

notes: Conflicts with the same report's running text (p.15) '53% of the value added' (CLM-0477).
